description: Capability for the main window. Notes: opener:allow-open-path exists for the attachments feature (src/services/attachments/file-actions.ts) — opening downloaded/cache files with the OS default app. It is path-scoped to $APPDATA/attachment_cache/** — the attachment cache subtree every openPath call site targets (verified: file-actions.ts resolves only <appData>/attachment_cache paths). Scoping matters: fs:allow-appdata-write-recursive lets the webview write anywhere under $APPDATA, so a wider opener scope (the former $APPDATA/**) would let any webview compromise write an executable into app data and open it with the OS handler. http:default is limited to the six API hosts the TS clients fetch (plain webview fetch — the app never routes through the plugin's fetch command): oauth2.googleapis.com + gmail.googleapis.com + www.googleapis.com (Gmail REST/token + Google Calendar, token-manager.ts, gmail-api.ts, add-gmail.ts, calendar/), login.microsoftonline.com + graph.microsoft.com (Microsoft mail + calendar, microsoft-oauth.ts, microsoft-calendar.ts), and www.virustotal.com for the opt-in attachment malware hash lookup (src/services/attachments/malware-lookup.ts — hash-only GETs, no content upload). Two layers gate outbound HTTPS and they mirror each other: the webview's own fetch is governed by the CSP connect-src in tauri.conf.json, while this allow-list governs the http plugin's IPC fetch surface — which application code does not use but a compromised webview COULD invoke directly, so an unbounded entry here would hand script execution in the webview an arbitrary-host fetch primitive (Rust-side, CORS-free). The OAuth authorization URL is opened in the system browser, not via plugin-http. There is deliberately NO wildcard entry: the former https://* existed for the RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe POST (task 18.3, security/unsubscribe.ts), whose List-Unsubscribe targets are owned by arbitrary mailing-list servers — that request now travels through the `unsubscribe_one_click_post` Rust command (src-tauri/src/unsubscribe.rs), which validates the URL (https, no userinfo/fragment/control chars, no redirects, no credentials) and issues the POST itself, so the webview never needs an arbitrary-host fetch capability. sql:default is read-only (close/load/select); sql:allow-execute is required because the DB layer writes (migrations, message ingestion, settings) through database.execute — without it every write is ACL-denied in the packaged app (the mock harness masks this by replacing plugin-sql). fs:allow-open exists for data portability (tasks 19.2–19.4): the mbox exporter streams through a plugin-fs file handle (`open`, src/services/data-portability/mbox.ts) — its sibling write commands (write/remove) already ride fs:allow-appdata-write-recursive's write-all set, but `open` sits in the fs command model's read family and needs this permission. The command stays path-scope-gated at runtime — the dialog plugin adds every picked/saved path to the fs scope for the session (unpersisted; see @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog dist-js) — so no $HOME scope is granted. The import parser reads picked .eml/.mbox files Rust-side (mail_import.rs std::fs), needs no fs permission, and additionally gates the read on app.fs_scope().is_allowed(path) so a compromised webview cannot use the import commands to parse arbitrary on-disk mail archives. The five window/webview entries after start-dragging exist for the composer pop-out window (batch C2, composer-popout.tsx + services/desktop/popout.ts openComposerPopout): the window is created from the JS WebviewWindow API with a `popout-composer-<draftKey>` label (already covered by the popout-* window pattern above) — allow-create-webview-window creates it, allow-get-all-windows powers the getByLabel reuse check, and show/set-focus/unminimize focus an existing composer pop-out instead of stacking a second one.
